title: Fugaro credential route
description: One repository's credential-route record: the node a member's own `fugaro update` publishes under config/policy/route/<slug> and a run of that repository reads once at its start, naming the service each kind of its credentials is served from -- its own project's credentials service, or the workspace's (docs/workspace-service/implementation-plan.md C2, reconciliation R3 and R4). It is a record and not a document, so it is closed: a key outside the members below is refused, because the record moves a member's credential from one service to another and a key nobody read is a decision nobody made. The address travels in this record and never in a job or launch variable (R3): it is the fifth field of the member's own workspace pin, and the run mints an identity token for whatever address the record it read carries. A repository with no record at all is served by the project's own service, which is today's behaviour, so a member in no workspace publishes nothing.

version.$comment: RouteVersion in internal/creds/route.go. A reader refuses a version it does not know rather than reading what it recognises, so this const and that constant move together.

address.description: The workspace's credentials service, from the member's own pin (R3). A scheme and a host only, with no user, path, query or fragment, and never http off loopback: the run mints an identity token for this address and sends the member's own token to it. The workspace is never the source of it -- a workspace that could name the address its members call could move every member's calls. Every record carries it, and it is not a promise that the workspace serves something: a record may name every kind the project's, and its address is then never called, because only an explicit `workspace` holder sends a call there.

model.description: Where the model credentials a run's calls go out on are served from.

bitbucket.description: Where the Bitbucket credential a repository's git traffic uses is served from.

github.description: Where the GitHub App the run's tokens are minted with is served from.

holder.description: HolderProject or HolderWorkspace in internal/creds/route.go. `workspace` means the workspace's service serves this kind for this repository, under the workspace entry's allow-list, the member's own policy and the repository's admission (R5); `project` means the member's own service does, which is also the answer for a kind the record does not name at all -- a kind the record leaves out is not a third state, it is the project's. Only an explicit `workspace` moves a kind, so a record that is truncated or half-understood cannot send a call anywhere but the project.
